shared_context.content: A sequence g_1,...,g_d of homogeneous elements of a graded ring is called a homogeneous regular sequence if for every i with 1 <= i <= d, multiplication by the image of g_i on S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is injective; equivalently, that image is not a zero-divisor there.
shared_context.label: Homogeneous regular sequence

strategy_summary: Local regular-ring strategy: isolate the full-ideal branch as a bottleneck, and in the proper-ideal branch localize at the homogeneous maximal ideal m=(x_1,...,x_d). Finite-dimensionality makes the localized quotient finite length, S_m is regular local of dimension d, so the localized sequence is regular. Then descend injectivity from the localization back to the original graded quotients using a graded local-to-global injectivity lemma.
